logo_override.validation_detail: png, probed via webfetch -> 'Image fetched successfully' (HTTP 200 + image content type); 'Yale University' wordmark in Yale's own letterforms, rendered near-black on a transparent background so it stays legible on a light card

notes: Awarding body is Yale University, so the Yale University mark is correct. The stored official_source_url finaid.yale.edu/apply/prospective fetched fine but carries NO logo image at all: it runs the yalesites 'atomic' theme whose site-branding is plain text ('Undergraduate Financial Aid' / 'Yale University') and whose footer brand is the literal character  rendered from a webfont, not an asset. Its only images are a Rose Walk campus photo and favicons at /profiles/custom/yalesites_profile/modules/custom/ys_media/images/favicons/* (the bare Yale 'Y' tile). So I went to the parent domain www.yale.edu, which rule 1 explicitly allows. The yale.edu homepage header publishes its official site logo as ; probed it and it is a real PNG (200 + image content type). Rule 3 matters here and is satisfied: the on-screen Yale Blue header logo is white-on-blue, but this file is the print variant, which is the dark/black wordmark - the brief's 'if the only variant is white, hunt for a dark one' case, and I picked the dark one deliberately. Checked the theme stylesheet /sites/all/themes/yale_blue/css/site.css for a larger or colour variant and it contains no url(...) logo reference at all, and brand.yale.edu is unreachable from here (transport error), so this print wordmark is the best on-domain Yale mark.
